The target video is 16:9 live-action with the intimate, lively, slightly uncontrolled urban-memory character of <Subject 3>. Handheld movement must always arise from the camera operator’s footsteps, retreat, tilt reaction, or attempt to reacquire <Subject 1>; never use random vibration, stabilized gimbal movement, orbiting, slow motion, or rigid central symmetry. Preserve normal action speed. No dialogue, narration, speech-like mouth movements, subtitles, readable added text, logos, or watermarks.

[Shot 1] The video begins directly from <Picture 1>. From 00:00.000 to 00:04.000, a close medium shot at chest height frames <Subject 1> leaning beside the glass shelter, with the left doorframe and glass edge retained in the foreground. She wears the ivory knit top and dark trousers and holds the light coat tightly against one shoulder. After a brief beat, she suddenly leans her upper body out from beside the frame, turns quickly toward the lens, and takes one cheerful step closer as her smile opens naturally. Her free arm swings outward; her long hair whips broadly with the turn, and the knit fabric and bundled coat shift visibly. The camera instinctively retreats about 40 centimeters, producing one step-driven vertical bump and a hurried correction that briefly crops the top of her head before recovering her face. Warm lights behind the glass slide through the reflection. End with her leaning toward the camera, smiling fully. A crisp snare accent lands with her turn. Add shoe movement, cloth friction, and a light glass-door rattle.

[Shot 2] At 00:04.000, hard cut to <Picture 2>. Use a close 25mm first-person perspective with the left and right doorframes as fixed spatial references. <Subject 1> now wears the black dress, oversized beige coat, shoulder bag, and black shoes. From her current half-crouch, she rises quickly and takes two normal-speed steps toward the lens. She first sweeps loose hair away from her face with her right hand, then extends that hand naturally toward the camera as if pulling the camera operator along. Her coat, skirt, bag, and hair lift strongly with the motion. The camera backs away about 80 centimeters with readable footstep bounce, lateral sway, a momentary focus miss, and rapid facial reacquisition. Background headlights slide laterally into short motion streaks; all vehicles remain distant. End with her hand close to the lens and her torso leaning forward. A rising bass figure enters as she stands. Add quick footsteps, coat flutter, and a brief rush of hair near the microphone.

[Shot 3] At 00:08.000, her approaching hand partially occludes the lens and motivates a hard cut to <Picture 3>. A low, close viewpoint retains the pale-grey wall and doorframe on the left and <Subject 2> at lower left. <Subject 1> now wears the oversized dark-grey blazer, pale satin camisole, grey trousers, and black shoes. Still crouching, she quickly offers a small piece of food toward the cat; the cat takes one natural step forward and sniffs. She withdraws her hand, smiles silently, rises only halfway, and turns toward the lens while supporting herself with her other hand on her knee. Her hair slides from her shoulder and swings sideways, and the blazer hem flicks outward. The camera first tilts down to follow the offered food, then rapidly corrects upward with an operator-driven wobble and short focus loss. Do not let her stand fully. End with her halfway upright, facing the camera while the cat remains beside her feet. Briefly reduce the drums as she looks up. Add cat paws on pavement, a soft food-wrapper rustle, and clothing movement.

[Shot 4] At 00:12.000, use a four-to-six-frame frontal-flash overexposure burst to transition into <Picture 4>. Exposure immediately returns to the same high-contrast flash aesthetic. From 00:12.000 to 00:14.500, the camera tracks from close behind and slightly beside <Subject 1> while moving forward with her. She now wears the dark blazer, pale satin long skirt, and black boots and holds a newspaper overhead against the rain. She looks back and laughs visually with an open joyful expression but produces no clear vocal sound or speech, then turns toward screen-right and runs two to three quick steps. One hand keeps the newspaper overhead while the other lifts part of the skirt. Wet hair, blazer, satin skirt, and newspaper flap strongly; rainwater runs from the paper’s edges. The operator follows for about one meter with pronounced running bounce, lateral sway, temporary focus loss, and hurried reframing while keeping her identifiable. Red traffic lights and white headlights stretch across the wet road; vehicles remain distant and never approach her. The complete drum groove returns when she starts running.

From 00:14.500 to 00:15.000, the camera deliberately stops and lets her continue toward screen-right. Her skirt sweeps across the edge of the frame as she nearly exits. Cut directly to black at 00:14.500; the music stops cleanly with the cut. Hold black for the remaining half-second with only rain and a faint, distant, unvoiced breathy exhale suggesting residual laughter. No clear human voice.

detailed_description:
Photorealistic cinematic drama in 16:9, with natural skin texture, soft highlights, shallow depth of field, and restrained acting. Use hard cuts between viewpoints. The man is one ordinary stranger throughout; changing visibility reveals his existing face rather than transforming it.

[Shot 1] A medium close-up with a 50mm lens frames <Subject 1> alone at the counter in <Subject 2>, following <Picture 1>. From 00:00.000 to 00:04.000, the camera slowly pushes in with very small amplitude and barely perceptible handheld movement. One hand supports her cheek while the other slowly rotates <Subject 3> on the counter. She looks down at the whiskey, shoulders slightly drawn inward, her movements tired and unhurried. Warm amber light falls across her face from the established side; background patrons dissolve into soft bokeh. Ice gently touches the glass. Near the end, a brief swell of activity from the dance floor catches her attention. Her glass-hand stops moving.

[Shot 2] At 00:04.000, hard cut to a profile close-up on the same side of the action axis. Her eyes lift first, followed by a slow turn and lift of her head toward the dance floor. Her unfocused gaze briefly sharpens. Her breathing pauses for half a beat as a purple-blue light passes across her eyes. A small trace of anticipation appears without a broad smile. Establish this gaze direction consistently for the following point-of-view shot.

[Shot 3] At 00:06.000, hard cut to her seated-eye-height point of view, using a 70–85mm lens and shallow depth of field. Magenta, indigo, cyan, and amber lights sweep across a crowded dance floor. Moving dancers leave subtle motion trails. Deep within the crowd, a man in a dark jacket is already present, initially seen from behind. His build and silhouette suggest someone familiar. Passing dancers repeatedly obscure him as he advances a few steps toward the foreground. The camera drifts slightly and makes small searching focus adjustments. His partial profile remains indistinct through backlight, haze, and defocus. Near the end, a brief warm-white light illuminates his face as focus settles, revealing a stranger. He does not look into the lens. He turns and disappears naturally behind the dancers, without teleporting or changing appearance.

[Shot 4] At 00:10.000, hard cut to a frontal close-up of <Subject 1>, framed to include her glass-hand and the counter. The camera now remains still. She watches the man's exit direction for half a second; anticipation slowly leaves her eyes. She looks away, and a barely perceptible, self-mocking smile appears at one corner of her mouth. A single tear slips from her lower eyelid down her cheek. She leaves it untouched and slowly lowers her head.

From 00:13.000 to 00:15.000, within the same shot, her fingers tighten around <Subject 3>. She lifts it, drinks the small remaining mouthful in one motion, and returns it to its original counter position with a clear clink. The whiskey is gone, but the ice remains. Hold the final moment on her lowered, dimmed gaze while the surrounding bar stays busy. No exaggerated sobbing, dialogue, voiceover, or subtitles.

They return to their normal level as she finishes the drink, with the final glass clink clearly audible above them.
